126	     installed types.

132	     typecheck — but state this plainly in your reply: *"typecheck skipped by

137	     screen in both `light` and `dark` themes (text and controls on colored
138	     fills especially), narrow (~375px) and wide (~1400px) viewports for
139	     horizontal overflow, and empty / loading / error states.

141	## Hard rules
142	
143	- **`@gravity-ui/uikit` MUST be installed in every Gravity UI project.** It is
144	  the base component + design-token library every other `@gravity-ui/*` package
145	  builds on; without it components render unstyled. If `package.json` lacks it,
146	  stop and have the user install and configure it first (setup:
147	  `https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt`).
148	- **Read `package.json` before importing any `@gravity-ui/*` package.** Never
149	  assume a package is installed; never assume its major version.
150	- **Do not invent props or components.** Before using a component API you are
151	  not 100% sure of, check `rules/hallucination-traps.md` (ecosystem patterns)
152	  and the component's README in `dist/docs`. If still unsure, ask the user
153	  rather than guessing.
154	- **Never guess icon names** — they are hallucinated more often than not. To
155	  match an icon from a screenshot/photo/mock, run `scripts/icon-image-search.sh`
156	  (reverse image search). With only a description, look the name up on
157	  `gravity-ui.com/icons` or ask the user — do not invent one. Then pass it as an
158	  object (`<Icon data={CheckIcon} />`), never a string key. See
159	  `references/icons.md`.
160	- **Theming uses semantic `--g-*` tokens.** Never hardcode colors (`#fff`,
161	  `blue-500`); never hand-write `dark:` overrides. Full token tables live in
162	  `references/theming.md`; the cross-cutting traps (partial brand overrides,
163	  a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, controls on a brand background) live in
164	  `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
165	- **Required setup is package-specific** (style imports, `ThemeProvider`,
166	  peer-deps). It lives in each package's root README under "Required setup" —
167	  read it once per package, do not rely on memory.
168

172	already implied by the rules above; this section exists as an explicit
173	stop-sign. If you are about to do any of these, stop and re-ground.
174

176	  `<input>`/`<button>`, or look-alike component libs. Use the `@gravity-ui/*`
177	  package the task needs.
178	- **Do not invent component APIs or props.** If a prop is not in the docs you
179	  read in Step 1, it does not exist — do not write `variant=`, `color=`,
180	  `name=` (on `Icon`), or a `header-3` variant. Use the documented prop or
181	  ask the user. See `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
182	- **Do not use the `/llms/<pkg>/llms.txt` "latest" alias as a fallback.** It
183	  serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
184	  different API. The versioned online fallback is the major-line URL
185	  (`/llms/<pkg>/<major>/llms.txt`); below that, go LOCAL.
186	- **Do not partial-brand.** Setting only `--g-color-base-brand` leaves
187	  selection, focus, links and contrast on the default accent — a mismatched
188	  UI. Override the full brand token set, on each theme you support.
189	- **Do not override internal markup with `[class*='…']` / ID selectors.**
190	  That's written against one DOM structure and breaks silently when the
191	  component changes. Climb the customization ladder
192	  (global token → component CSS API → narrow flagged hack) before ever
193	  touching structure.
194

196	
197	These files live alongside this SKILL.md and load only when relevant:
198	
199	- `references/package-routing.md` — offline snapshot of the ecosystem catalog
200	  (`gravity-ui.com/llms.txt`), refreshed each skill release. Used as the
201	  offline fallback in Step 0.
202	- `references/theming.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/theming.md`:
203	  `--g-*` token layers, `ThemeProvider`, branding, custom themes, scoped
204	  themes, `uikit-themer`. The bundled copy may lag — read
205	  `node_modules/@gravity-ui/uikit/build/docs/guides/theming.md` for the
206	  version-matched file.
207	- `references/layout.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/layout.md`:
208	  spacing scale (`--g-spacing-*`), `Flex`/`Box`, `Row`/`Col`/`Container`
209	  grid, breakpoints, `useLayoutContext`.
210	- `references/icons.md` — finding an icon by image
211	  (`scripts/icon-image-search.sh`) or on gravity-ui.com/icons; the
212	  object-vs-string rendering rule.
213	- `rules/hallucination-traps.md` — Incorrect/Correct pairs for the most
214	  commonly invented APIs: typography variants (`header-3..6` don't exist, no
215	  `Heading`), the flex contract (`min-width:0`, who shrinks), theming traps
216	  (partial brand overrides, a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, customization
217	  ladder), `Button view` not `variant`, `Icon data` not `name`. Per-component
218	  traps live in each package's `dist/docs`, not here.

1	# TextInput
2	
3	```tsx
4	import {TextInput} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
5	```
6	
7	TextInput allow users to enter text into a UI.
8	
9	## Appearance
10	
11	The appearance of `TextInput` is controlled by the `view` and `pin` properties.
12	
13	### View
14	
15	`normal` - the main view of `TextInput` (used by default).
16	
17	`clear` - can be used with a custom wrapper for `TextInput`.
18	
19	```tsx
20	<TextInput view="normal" />
21	<TextInput view="clear" />
22	```
23	
24	### Pin
25	
26	Allows you to control view of right and left edges of `TextInput`'s border.
27	
28	```tsx
29	<TextInput pin="round-brick" />
30	<TextInput pin="brick-brick" />
31	<TextInput pin="brick-round" />
32	```
33	
34	## States
35	
36	### Disabled
37	
38	The state of the `TextInput` where you don't want the user to be able to interact with the component.
39	
40	```tsx
41	<TextInput disabled />
42	```
43	
44	### Error
45	
46	The state of the `TextInput` in which you want to indicate incorrect user input. To change `TextInput` appearance, use the `validationState` property with the `"invalid"` value. An optional message text can be added via the `errorMessage` property. By default, message text is rendered outside the component.
47	This behaviour can be changed with the `errorPlacement` property.
48	
49	```tsx
50	<TextInput errorMessage="Error message" validationState="invalid" />
51	<TextInput errorPlacement="inside" errorMessage="Error message" validationState="invalid" />
52	```
53	
54	## Size
55	
56	`s` – Used when standard controls are too big (tables, small cards).
57	
58	`m` – Basic size, used in most components.
59	
60	`l` – Basic controls performed in a page's header, modal windows, or pop-ups.
61	
62	`xl` – Used on promo and landing pages.
63	
64	```tsx
65	<TextInput size="s" />
66	<TextInput size="m" />
67	<TextInput size="l" />
68	<TextInput size="xl" />
69	```
70	
71	## Label
72	
73	Allows you to set the label to the left of control.
74	
75	- label occupies the leftmost position relative to the control. That is, the elements added via `startContent` property will be located to the right.
76	- label can take up no more than half the width of the entire TextInput's space.
77	
78	```tsx
79	<TextInput label="Label" />
80	```
81	
82	## Additional content
83	
84	### Start content
85	
86	Allows you to add content to the left of the control (or to the right in case of using [rtl](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/RTL)). Located to the left (or to the right in case of using rtl) of the label added via `label` property.
87	
88	```tsx
89	<TextInput startContent={<Label>Left</Label>} />
90	```
91	
92	### End content
93	
94	Allows you to add content to the right (or to the left in case of using [rtl](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/RTL)) of the control. Located to the right (or to the left in case of using rtl) of the clear button added via `hasClear` property.
95	
96	```tsx
97	<TextInput endContent={<Label>Right</Label>} />
98	```

106	| className       | The control's wrapper class name                                                                                        |                               `string`                                |                 |
107	| controlProps    | The control's html attributes                                                                                           |             `React.InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement>`             |                 |
108	| controlRef      | React ref provided to the control                                                                                       |                     `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>`                     |                 |
109	| defaultValue    | The control's default value, used when the component is not controlled                                                  |                               `string`                                |                 |

111	| endContent      | User`s node rendered after input node, clear button and error icon                                                      |                               `string`                                |                 |
112	| errorMessage    | Error text                                                                                                              |                               `string`                                |                 |

[English](./theming.md) | [Русский](./theming-ru.md)

We use and recommend CSS variables for theming.

Everything is driven by CSS custom properties prefixed with `--g-*`. There is no runtime styling API you need to call — you set variables and components pick them up.

```tsx
import {Provider, Button} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/fonts.css';
import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css';

  <Provider theme="system">
    <Button view="action">Branded button</Button>
  </Provider>
);

All variables live on the root class `.g-root`, which `ThemeProvider` assigns to `<body>` by
default when used without a parent theme (use `scoped` for a local root). Color variables additionally live on a
per-theme class `.g-root_theme_{themeName}`, so switching the theme swaps one set of values for
another.

```
.g-root                      → structural tokens (spacing, typography metrics, border radius)
.g-root_theme_light          → color tokens for the light theme
.g-root_theme_dark           → color tokens for the dark theme
```

several themes, or globally. If you support more than one theme, set color overrides **per theme**.

# Card

`Card` is a reusable React component that basically is a card-like container with customizable styles and features. It is used to display information or content in a visually appealing and well-organized manner.

```tsx
import {Card} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
```

## Appearance

`Card` can be displayed with multiple style combinations:

- `theme`: `normal`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, or `utility`.
- `type`: `selection`, `action`, or `container`.
- `view`:`outlined` or `clear`, or `outlined`, `filled`, or `raised` (depending on the `type` parameter).

## Theme

This parameter is used to specify the card's theme style. It determines the card's color scheme and appearance.

By specifying different theme values, you can customize the `Card` visual appearance to match your purpose and the style you need.

- `normal`: Normal/default theme of the card.
- `info`: Theme for displaying neutral information.
- `success`: Theme for displaying positive or affirmative content.
- `warning`: Theme for displaying warnings.
- `danger`: Theme for displaying the content related to critical issues or errors.
- `utility`: Theme for displaying useful tips.

## Type

This parameter is used to define the type of the `Card` component. It allows you to customize the appearance and behavior of the card.

- `container`: Card that acts as a container for other elements. It provides a structured layout for content.
- `action`: Card with an interactive element, such as a button, that triggers an action when clicked.
- `selection`: Card that can be selected or clicked to perform a specific action.

## View

This parameter is used to specify the `Card` view or layout style. It allows you to customize the appearance and arrangement of the card content.

- `clear`: No style.
- `outlined`: Applies a thin border to highlight the card content.
- `filled`: Fills in the card content.
- `raised`: Applies a shadow to slightly lift the container.
